title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}, a free profinite group of rank 2. Ŝ^+_{0,3} ≃ (P)SL(2,Z)^ contains π̂_{0,3} as a normal subgroup with quotient S_3; this is the profinite completion of Γ(2)/±1 ⊂ PSL(2,Z). M̃_{0,3} is the group of automorphisms of Ŝ^+_{0,3} that preserve π̂_{0,3} and the 'loop structure': each inertia generator ξ_i is sent to a conjugate of ξ_i^μ, μ ∈ Ẑ^*. Ñ_{0,3} = M̃_{0,3}/π̂_{0,3} is identified with the group of outer loop-automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} commuting with the outer S_3-action.

This page continues that bookkeeping.
(5) M̃ → Aut(S_3) = S_3. This uses (4), Inn(S_3) = Aut(S_3).
(7) The map is trivial on π̂, since conjugation by f ∈ π̂ induces conjugation by the trivial image in S_3. So it factors through Ñ → S_3.
(8), (9) The kernels M̃^!, Ñ^! give two exact rows. Row (9) is row (8) divided by π̂, and (9bis) 1 → π̂ → M̃^! → Ñ^! → 1.
(10) The canonical section is S_3 = Ŝ^+/π̂ → Ñ, induced by inner automorphisms of Ŝ^+. Its composite with (7) is the identity, because int(x) induces int(x̄) on S_3.
(11) Hence Ñ ≃ S_3 × Ñ^!. This is a direct, not merely semidirect, product: the image of S_3 is Inn(Ŝ^+)/Inn(π̂), which is normal in Ñ. Ñ^! is a kernel, hence normal. The two meet trivially and generate.
(12) The finite 'Teichmüller' group T_{0,3} ≃ S_3 × Z/2 (the extended mapping class group / symmetries of the tripod, including orientation reversal) embeds in Ñ. T^+ = S_3 maps via (10). T^! = Z/2 = ⟨τ⟩ goes into the factor Ñ^!, with τ the orientation-reversing element (complex conjugation).
The next page adds the character χ: Ñ → Ẑ^* (with τ ↦ −1) and the embedding Γ_Q ↪ Ñ^! (Belyi/Ihara). Overall this is the standard framework in which GT̂ sits as a subgroup of Ñ^!, here before imposing pentagon/hexagon-type relations.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Product decomposition (11) is genuinely direct, as argued, though the page does not spell out why it is not merely semidirect.
Notation is inconsistent: M̃^! versus M^{!~}, and T_{0,3} versus 𝒯_{0,3}. Ŝ^+ ≃ SL(2,Z)^ should be read as PSL(2,Z)^ (the prime in the previous page's 'SL(2,Z)^∧′' likely signals this).

ideas.what: Group of S_3-equivariant inertia-preserving ('à lacets') outer automorphisms of the free profinite group of rank 2, as automorphisms of PSL(2,Z)^ normalizing F̂_2
ideas.modern_name: Ambient group of GT̂; inertia-preserving outer automorphisms Out^♯(F̂_2) commuting with S_3 (Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps setting)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s), Nakamura; idea of Gal(Q̄/Q) acting on the tower from Grothendieck's Esquisse (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (conceptually); details in La Longue Marche (circulated 1981) unsure

ideas.what: Splitting Ñ ≃ S_3 × Ñ^! via inner automorphisms of PSL(2,Z)^
ideas.modern_name: Standard reduction from the S_3-normalizer to the centralizer; GT̂ commutes with S_3

ideas.what: Embedding of S_3 × Z/2 (with complex conjugation τ in the Ñ^! factor)
ideas.modern_name: Complex conjugation as element (−1,1) of GT̂; extended mapping class group of M_{0,3}-tripod

deep.surprise_reason: Careful notational bookkeeping of standard group-theoretic facts in the GT̂ ambient setting; no new result, construction or connection beyond what is now standard.
transcription_corrections: Label (9bis) and the inserted line read 'Notons aussi la structure abstraite correspondante' – plausible, but 'abstraite' is uncertain ('extension' possible).
In (12) the group is written as a calligraphic/Gothic 𝒯_{0,3}, not plain T_{0,3}; the marginal additions are '= 𝒯^+_{0,3}' and '𝒯^!_{0,3} ='.
Superscript order varies between the image (Ñ^{!~}) and the transcription (N^{~!}); these denote the same object.
